correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md sentence has four variable names and rank four, expresses no isolated vertices and closure of distinct adjacency rows under XOR. Distinct rows follow since an equal pair would force the forbidden zero row; adjoining zero makes a vector space over F2. Symmetric, loopless adjacency defines an alternating bilinear form, nondegenerate because each nonzero row has a neighbor. Even-dimensional symplectic graphs satisfy the sentence in reverse. Optimality: the explicitly published 63-vertex Godsil–McKay switch has the same (63,32,16,16) strongly regular parameters, binary adjacency ranks 8 versus 6 and all two-fixed-vertex adjacency cells nonempty, yielding unrestricted three-pebble equivalence but nonmembership. Independently built the 63-vertex graphs, switched edges, verified rank 6/8 and row XOR closure discrepancy. The finite verification corroborates the unrestricted-depth pebble proof, not a substitute for it.
